name: Scapular Push-Up on Floor
description: The scapular push-up isolates the serratus anterior by performing the protraction-retraction movement of the scapulae while maintaining a rigid plank position. Unlike a standard push-up, the elbows remain fully locked throughout the movement — only the shoulder blades move. This exercise is a cornerstone of shoulder rehabilitation for winging scapula, rotator cuff issues, and overhead athlete conditioning.

execution.starting_position: Assume a standard push-up position with arms fully extended, hands directly under shoulders. Keep the entire body rigid from head to heels.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Ensure a non-slip surface. Can be performed from knees for a modified version.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a push-up plank with elbows fully locked. Do not bend the elbows at any point.
Step 2: Allow the chest to drop between the shoulder blades by letting the scapulae retract (pinch together).
Step 3: Push the floor away with both hands to protract the scapulae, making the upper back rounded and scapulae spread wide.
Step 4: Hold the protracted position briefly, then return to retraction. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you protract (spread the shoulder blades). Inhale as you retract (pinch them together).
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — this converts it into a regular push-up
Losing the rigid plank body position and sagging at the hips
Moving too quickly — slow movement ensures scapular isolation
safety_considerations: Avoid with acute shoulder impingement presenting with protraction pain
Consult a physiotherapist if you have diagnosed scapular winging
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: The range is relatively small — focus on maximum protraction vs. retraction of the shoulder blades, not on raising or lowering the torso.
coaching_cues: Arms stay straight throughout — only the shoulder blades move
Push the floor away as hard as possible at the top
Think about spreading the shoulder blades wide like wings
